sense: one’s own, private: not public or official

terms.gloss: personal, private, one’s own (as against public or official)
evidence: Cic. Sen. 22: in vītā etiam prīvātā et quiētā
Cic. Quinct. 15: rēs quae ipsīus erant prīvātae, his personal property (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The opposite of pūblicus. Personal life is vīta prīvāta; as a noun, prīvātus is a private citizen (see individual). A personal opinion is simply one’s own: mea sententia (see own).
To someone’s face is also cōram (Ter. Ad. 269).

terms.gloss: of a person (in law); personal (in grammar)
terms.comment: A lawyers’ and grammarians’ word: an action against a person, a personal verb or pronoun. Classically a persōna is a mask or a part played, not one’s private self.

phrases.latin: manent ingenia senibus, modo permaneat studium et industria, neque ea sōlum clārīs et honōrātīs virīs, sed in vītā etiam prīvātā et quiētā
phrases.english: old men keep their wits, so long as their interest and diligence last, and not only famous men who have held office, but also in a quiet private life
I’d rather hear it from you in person

phrases.latin: vereor cōram in ōs tē laudāre amplius
phrases.english: I’m shy of praising you any more to your face
